# Modified OpenHMD acquisition engine

Source: [Jan Schmidt's OpenHMD fork](https://github.com/thaytan/OpenHMD), branch `rift-kalman-filter`, commit [`a4ebf094e8be5c53c43c5f68d92e87afa5bdf0c8`](https://github.com/thaytan/OpenHMD/commit/a4ebf094e8be5c53c43c5f68d92e87afa5bdf0c8), dated 2026-07-29 ("rift: Backport pose metric tweaks from Monado"). Imported as source, without upstream history; this is a modified snapshot, not an unmodified upstream release.

Most source is under Boost Software License 1.0; dual-license files are used under their Boost option. `nxjson` retains MIT, and `miniz` retains Unlicense/public-domain terms. See the individual source headers, this directory's `LICENSE`, and the root `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. The unused upstream GStreamer plugin and 3Glasses driver are omitted; other upstream hardware sources are retained but only the Rift driver is configured by cv1touch.

Local changes expose a bounded CV1 acquisition API, controller/radio decoding, factory geometry, timestamps, raw/labelled observations, optional PipeWire views, fixed calibrated camera poses, radio-only headset operation, and more resilient camera transfers. Tracking for cv1touch is performed in Rust. Native dependencies are resolved from the system. The small nxjson UTF-8 encoder is replaced with an independently written Unicode-scalar encoder and boundary tests.

Compare this snapshot against the pinned upstream commit to inspect the complete modification set. Subsequent release changes are tracked in this repository. Preserve upstream notices when modifying or extracting code.

## Local changes

These are summaries; the code and its native tests (`tests/test_*.c` at the repository root) are the reference.

- **Stream shutdown.** The UVC stop flag is atomic, and teardown signals every stream before changing a USB alternate setting or waiting for transfers. Failed submissions are parked and retried at most once per 10 ms, so a peer's retry loop cannot block shutdown. Failures a stop causes itself, such as clearing the alternate setting of an unplugged sensor, are not reported.
- **Factory-calibration identity.** The CV1 extension exposes each controller's cached factory-calibration identity, so user input calibration is bound to that controller. Analog values stay unbounded at acquisition; the daemon applies correction and bounds them.
- **Dynamic sensors.** Discovery keeps a dynamically sized registry with no fixed sensor count. A separate setter deep-copies the ignore and pose lists without changing the scalar configuration ABI. Discovery rejects unusable or duplicate identities, cleans up failed starts, and keeps frame storage until analysis workers have joined.
- **Logging.** The engine logs to its C runtime's stdout. `ohmd_cv1touch_unbuffer_log` turns its buffering off; the daemon calls it on Windows, where the library's own runtime fully buffers a pipe or file.
- **Blob extraction.** `rift-sensor-blobwatch.c` handles the first scanline without reading a null previous line (`blobwatch_ubsan` checks this under UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer).
- **Frame validation.** UVC assembly rejects incomplete raw images and damaged header, frame-ID and timestamp sequences before delivery. A leftover packet from an earlier stream no longer causes the first image of a new stream to be rejected. JPEG images end at an outer EOI after SOS or at EOF, with marker payloads skipped by length. JPEG decoding rejects the libjpeg warnings that mean concealed damage and keeps images with other warnings. Discarded images are logged as per-sensor summaries at most every 10 s. libjpeg-turbo can still decode some damaged data without a warning.
- **Video quality counters.** A separate 56-byte getter reports the negotiated raw or JPEG format, decoded JPEG images and rejected image candidates; the 40-byte acquisition record is unchanged.
- **Label inspection.** To check whether a sensor moved, an inspection keeps its calibrated pose for normal tracking and runs a private cold correspondence search for the requested controllers only. A candidate cannot label shared blobs, supply a fast prior or export a pose until its identity is established:
  - Identity belongs to one continuous correspondence: at least five unchanged blob/LED pairs across consecutive frames, no raw-frame gap over 60 ms, and each pair moving at most 32 px per frame.
  - The candidate's camera-relative rotation must follow that hand's IMU over at least 30 degrees and three agreeing exposures within 3 s, with error at most a tenth of the turn. If the other hand has IMU data, its turn must differ by at least half as much. This uses relative rotation only, not the disputed camera pose. Still, slow or identical two-hand motion cannot establish identity, and a swap during identical motion through an image overlap persists until the motions differ.
  - Three consecutive exposures that disagree with the IMU by more than ten degrees, or a tenth of the turn when larger, revoke the identity.
  - Each inspection has a 64-bit identity epoch tagged on its frames. A contradiction invalidates the epoch, and the daemon discards its checks and any delayed frames with that tag.
  - Labels found by the long search are queued and applied only by the fast worker between frames; a revoked identity removes them and its camera prior.
- **Search cancellation.** Pose restoration and sensor shutdown cancel correspondence searches at loop boundaries, and inspections have a native deadline. The extension acknowledges when a queued pose is applied and the previous search has stopped; the daemon holds its inspection slot until then.
- **Sensor retirement.** Retiring a sensor fences its pose submissions under its analysis lock and cancels its search; no new long search starts on it.
- **Attachment identity.** Last-start records hold a 16-byte attachment key in former reserved space (the record stays 64 bytes). On Linux the key is the inode of the sensor's sysfs directory, pinned with `O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC` before USB open; on Windows it is an instance and arrival snapshot taken before enumeration. An unknown or mismatched identity leaves the attachment pending instead of spending its start attempt.
- **Hot-plug.** `ohmd_cv1touch_add_sensor` queues an open on the engine's worker thread, `cv1t-sensors`, which checks the attachment key, opens and starts the sensor, and leaves it for `ohmd_cv1touch_poll_sensor_adds` to adopt on the engine thread. Frames exposed before the start returned are not searched for poses. `ohmd_cv1touch_release_sensor` retires a sensor and has the worker free it before opening another. Only the engine thread changes the roster; the lock order is roster, sensor, tracker, device, and no USB start, stop or retry runs under any of them.
